quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #12
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: What do fluorescent yellow-green signs indicate?

options.text: School zones.
Hospitals.
Speed limits.
Railroad crossings.

questions.correctAnswerText: School zones.
questions.explanation: Fluorescent yellow-green signs warn drivers about pedestrians, bicycles, and schools. Drive carefully when you see these signs.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: You must turn left or right.
You are approaching a T intersection.
Your road meets a divided highway.
You are on an overpass above a divided highway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your road meets a divided highway.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that your road crosses a divided highway. A divided highway has two one-way roads separated by a median or guard rail.

questions.question: When should you not pass?

options.text: On a hill or curve.
When school bus lights are flashing.
When approaching an intersection.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Never pass if you cannot see ahead clearly, if a school bus has its red lights flashing, at an intersection, at a railroad crossing, or on a bridge. Do not pass a stopped school bus with flashing red lights unless you are on the opposite side of a divided road.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Drive with caution and be ready to slow down.
Do not drive in this lane.
You must come to a complete stop and yield the right-of-way.
Slow down, be ready to stop, and yield the right-of-way if needed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down, be ready to stop, and yield the right-of-way if needed.
questions.explanation: This triangular sign means yield. Slow down at the intersection and be ready to stop. Let other vehicles, bicyclists, and pedestrians pass before you go.

questions.question: When can you go through a stop sign intersection with no stop line or crosswalk?

options.text: After slowing down to check for cross traffic.
After coming to a complete stop and making sure it is safe.
After stopping at least 20 feet before the intersection.
After slowing down to 10 mph.

questions.correctAnswerText: After coming to a complete stop and making sure it is safe.
questions.explanation: At a stop sign, stop before the stop line or crosswalk. If there is no stop line or crosswalk, stop before entering the intersection. Only go when it is safe.

questions.question: What is the safest way to drive in traffic?

options.text: Change your speed often to stay alert.
Drive faster than other traffic.
Drive slower than other traffic.
Drive with the flow of traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive with the flow of traffic.
questions.explanation: Crashes happen when drivers go much faster or slower than other cars. Drive at the same speed as traffic around you, staying within the posted speed limit.

questions.question: What affects how alcohol impacts your body?

options.text: The amount of food in your stomach.
Your body weight.
How much time passes between drinks.
All three of these.

questions.correctAnswerText: All three of these.
questions.explanation: Your blood alcohol level depends on how much you drink, the time between drinks, and your weight. Food in your stomach slows alcohol absorption, but it cannot prevent impairment from drinking too much.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: There is an object on the roadway.
Traffic is coming from the right.
The road curves sharply to the left.
There is a merge point ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road curves sharply to the left.
questions.explanation: This chevron sign shows a sharp curve in the direction of the arrow. The arrow points left, so the road curves left. Multiple chevron signs mark the entire curve.

questions.question: When may you use your horn?

options.text: When you have to stop quickly.
When you are passing another car.
When you have lost control of your car.
When you are passing a bicyclist.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you have lost control of your car.
questions.explanation: Use your horn when you lose control of your vehicle. This alerts other drivers to a dangerous situation.

questions.question: What do crossbuck signs indicate?

options.text: Railroad crossings.
School zones.
No passing zones.
Hospitals.

questions.correctAnswerText: Railroad crossings.
questions.explanation: Crossbuck signs mark railroad crossings. You must yield to trains at these crossings. Do not try to race a train across the tracks.

questions.question: If you see water covering the road, you should:

options.text: Drive until you think the water is too deep.
Drive through. The water is unlikely to be too deep.
Turn around and find another route.
Walk into the water to check how deep it is.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn around and find another route.
questions.explanation: Never drive through flooded roads. You cannot see how deep the water is or how fast it is moving. Your car could be swept away or sink.

questions.question: Motorcycles are allowed to use:

options.text: The bicycle lane.
The same full lane width as other motor vehicles.
Half the width of a lane.
The width of the sidewalk.

questions.correctAnswerText: The same full lane width as other motor vehicles.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have the right to use the full width of a lane, just like all other vehicles.

questions.question: When two drivers arrive at an open intersection at the same time:

options.text: The driver on the right has the right-of-way.
The driver on the left has the right-of-way.
One driver can go without stopping.
One driver should honk to show they are yielding.

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver on the right has the right-of-way.
questions.explanation: If you arrive at an open intersection at the same time as a vehicle to your right, let that vehicle go first. You can go when it is safe.

questions.question: A posted speed limit sign shows:

options.text: Only a suggested speed.
The exact speed you must drive to avoid a ticket.
The highest safe speed in good road and weather conditions.
The highest safe speed in all conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: The highest safe speed in good road and weather conditions.
questions.explanation: A speed limit is the maximum legal speed. You may need to drive slower than the limit when conditions are bad, such as during rain or snow.

questions.question: When turning right at a green light, you must:

options.text: Keep your normal speed.
Stop and look for police.
Yield to pedestrians.
Drive faster.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield to pedestrians.
questions.explanation: You can turn right or left at a green light unless a sign says you cannot. When turning, you must let other vehicles and pedestrians in the intersection go first.

questions.question: What does an orange sign mean?

options.text: A no passing zone is starting.
A railroad crossing is ahead.
A school zone is ahead.
Construction work is ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Construction work is ahead.
questions.explanation: Orange signs warn drivers about construction, maintenance, and emergency work.

questions.question: When you see an emergency vehicle with flashing lights, you must:

options.text: Slow down and stay in your lane.
Keep driving in your lane.
Move to the right side of the road and stop.
Stop right where you are.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the right side of the road and stop.
questions.explanation: When you see an emergency vehicle with flashing lights or hear its siren, pull over to the right side of the road and stop right away.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle, you should:

options.text: Check your mirrors and blind spots.
Honk your horn at least three times.
Move back into your lane within 10 feet of the other car.
You do not need to signal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your mirrors and blind spots.
questions.explanation: Before passing, check your mirrors and blind spots. Use your turn signal before changing lanes. Move back into your lane only after you can see the other car's front in your mirror.

questions.question: Drivers who eat or drink while driving:

options.text: Do not make any driving mistakes.
Have trouble driving slowly.
Are better drivers because they are not hungry.
Have trouble controlling their vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Have trouble controlling their vehicles.
questions.explanation: Eating, drinking, or smoking while driving is unsafe. These activities take your hands off the wheel and your eyes off the road. This makes it hard to stay in your lane and control your car.

questions.question: You can reduce the risk of hydroplaning by:

options.text: Driving through shallow water.
Driving faster.
Driving slower.
Driving through deep water.

questions.correctAnswerText: Driving slower.
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens when you drive too fast on wet roads. Driving slower reduces the chance of hydroplaning.

questions.question: You are driving on a two-lane road without bike lanes. A cyclist is ahead of you traveling in the same direction. What is the safest way to pass?

options.text: Slow down and wait for no oncoming traffic. Then pass while giving the cyclist plenty of space.
Keep driving straight. The cyclist must move out of your way.
Do not pass until you reach a traffic light or stop sign.
Honk to warn the cyclist you are passing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and wait for no oncoming traffic. Then pass while giving the cyclist plenty of space.
questions.explanation: Pass a cyclist like you would any other vehicle, but not too fast or close. Your speed and distance could blow debris or air at them. Leave at least 3 feet between your mirror and the cyclist. Use 5 feet on faster roads or when passing a group. Loud honking can startle cyclists and cause crashes.

questions.question: How do you stay out of a truck or bus driver's blind spot?

options.text: Never pass them.
Do not drive beside them and do not tailgate.
Flash your lights at them.
Honk your horn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not drive beside them and do not tailgate.
questions.explanation: Large vehicles like trucks and buses have large blind spots on the sides and rear. Avoid driving next to them and do not follow too closely.

questions.question: You are driving uphill and see a heavy truck ahead. You should know:

options.text: The truck may be going slower than the speed limit.
You may not be able to pass safely.
You may not be allowed to pass.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Large vehicles often go slower than the posted speed limit, especially uphill. Be careful when approaching from behind. On hills with poor visibility, passing another vehicle is illegal.

questions.question: Emergency vehicles:

options.text: Have the right-of-way when using sirens, horns, and flashing lights.
Can use a loudspeaker to give orders.
Can follow one another.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: You must let police cars, fire trucks, ambulances, and other emergency vehicles pass when they use a siren or air horn and red or blue lights. Follow their loudspeaker instructions. Emergency vehicles often follow each other, so only move when you are sure it is safe.

questions.question: Slow down below the speed limit when:

options.text: Anything makes driving conditions worse than normal.
You see a police car.
You enter a highway with other cars.
You are on a four-lane road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Anything makes driving conditions worse than normal.
questions.explanation: Drive slower when roads are wet or slippery, when you cannot see well, or when anything else makes conditions bad. Even if you obey the speed limit, you can get a ticket for driving too fast for the conditions.
